opening.quote: yeahs, hello, how could I help?
opening.comment: The agent never gave their own name or the company name in the opening turn; the first turn was a greeting only, with a stray customer-side phrasing.

verification.quote: Could eye take your fool name an your order lumber or
verification.comment: The agent asked for the full name and order number or postcode before sharing data, and the caller gave name and postcode, so verification was attempted; the transcript is garbled but the request was made.

understanding.quote: I've been charged price for mine order. at was €64.90 I see it twice on my statements.
understanding.comment: The agent correctly captured the duplicate charge of EUR 64.90 and did not re-ask for information the caller had already given.

resolution_accuracy.quote: I've €46.90 to your card today. It'll within 3 to 9 working days.
resolution_accuracy.comment: The policy says a duplicate charge is refunded in full the same day with the bank showing it in 3 to 5 working days; the agent stated the wrong refund amount (EUR 46.90 instead of EUR 64.90) and an incorrect timeline of 3 to 9 days.

process_compliance.quote: Thank you, mike. I could see the for a pair of cushion at €84.90, and two on a same day.
process_compliance.comment: No hold occurred and no photo or bank dispute handling applied, so no required step was missed; the duplicate refund itself needed no special process.

communication.quote: Sorry about that, I know that stressful to sea on you're statement.
communication.comment: The agent apologised and acknowledged the stress of the duplicate charge, though the transcript is garbled and the closing was curt.

closing.comment: The agent did not confirm clearly what happens next or ask if there was anything else, and the sign-off was cut off.
